general.q: Which is the longest river located entirely within England?
general.why: The Severn is the UK's longest river, but it starts in Wales, making the Thames the longest entirely in England.

general.q: What type of light pastry dough is used to make profiteroles and eclairs?
general.why: Choux pastry uses high moisture to create steam while baking, puffing it up into hollow treats.

general.q: Which planet in our solar system is orbited by the large moon Triton?
general.why: Triton is Neptune's largest moon and the only large moon in the Solar System with a retrograde orbit.

general.q: Which English monarch reigned for just nine days in July 1553?
general.why: Lady Jane Grey was proclaimed queen after Edward VI died, but was deposed by Mary I nine days later.

general.q: What is the hardest substance produced by the human body?
general.why: Tooth enamel is composed mostly of hydroxyapatite, making it significantly harder than human bone.

pop.q: In Only Fools and Horses, what specific vehicle model is Del Boy's yellow three-wheeled van?
pop.why: Though often confused with a Reliant Robin, Del Boy's famous van was actually a 1968 Reliant Regal.

pop.q: Which classic 1990s fighting game introduced the famous victory instruction "FINISH HIM!"?
pop.why: Mortal Kombat introduced the iconic phrase in 1992, prompting players to perform a gory Fatality move.

pop.q: Launched in 1996, which electronic virtual pet took its name from a blend of the Japanese words for 'egg' and 'watch'?
pop.why: Tamagotchi is a portmanteau combining the Japanese word 'tamago' (egg) with 'uotchi' (watch).

pop.q: In the famous 1990s UK television adverts for Tango soft drinks, what colour was the man who slapped consumers?
pop.why: The iconic 'You Know When You've Been Tango'd' advert featured a painted orange man slapping drink consumers.

pop.q: In the 1996 British film Trainspotting, what is the surname of Ewan McGregor's lead character, Mark?
pop.why: Ewan McGregor starred as Mark Renton, navigating the 1980s Edinburgh heroin scene.

music.q: In August 1995, Blur's single 'Country House' beat which Oasis song to the UK Number 1 spot?
music.why: The famous 'Battle of Britpop' saw Blur take the top spot, selling over 274,000 copies to Oasis's 216,000.

music.q: Which pop group achieved three consecutive UK Christmas Number 1 singles from 1996 to 1998?
music.why: They hit the UK Christmas top spot with '2 Become 1', 'Too Much', and 'Goodbye'.

music.q: Which song won the Eurovision Song Contest for the UK in 1997, performed by Katrina and the Waves?
a: Ooh Aah... Just a Little Bit
music.why: 'Love Shine a Light' scored 227 points, giving the UK its fifth Eurovision victory.

music.q: What was the title of American rock band The Killers' debut studio album, released in 2004?
music.why: Hot Fuss contained giant singles including 'Mr. Brightside' and 'Somebody Told Me'.

music.q: Which iconic Roland drum machine, launched in 1980, played a pivotal role in shaping hip-hop and dance music?
music.why: The TR-808 was famously used on tracks by Marvin Gaye, Afrika Bambaataa, and Whitney Houston.

mix.q: Which British band had a UK number one hit in 1995 with the single Country House?
mix.why: Blur beat Oasis to the top spot in August 1995 during the famous 'Battle of Britpop'.

mix.q: Which island is the largest by area in the Mediterranean Sea?
mix.why: Sicily is the largest island in the Mediterranean, sitting just ahead of Sardinia.

mix.q: Which 1994 film starring Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman was adapted from a Stephen King novella?
mix.why: It was based on Stephen King's 1982 novella Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption.

mix.q: What is the longest river located entirely within England?
mix.why: The Thames is the longest river entirely in England, as the longer Severn flows through Wales.

mix.q: Who sang lead vocals on the 1983 hit single Blue Monday by New Order?
mix.why: Bernard Sumner took over lead vocals for New Order following the death of Ian Curtis.

mix.q: Which UK comedy series featured the characters David Brent and Gareth Keenan?
mix.why: David Brent and Gareth Keenan were played by Ricky Gervais and Mackenzie Crook in The Office.

mix.q: What is the only chemical element that is liquid at standard room temperature and pressure besides mercury?
mix.why: Bromine is a reddish-brown halogen liquid and the only non-metallic element liquid at room temp.

mix.q: Which Swedish pop group had a UK number one single with The Winner Takes It All in 1980?
mix.why: ABBA scored nine UK number one singles, including The Winner Takes It All in August 1980.

mix.q: Which English king was defeated and killed at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485?
mix.why: Richard III was the last Plantagenet king and died fighting Henry Tudor's forces.

mix.q: In the 1999 movie The Matrix, what colour is the pill Neo takes to discover the truth?
mix.why: Morpheus offers Neo a choice between the blue pill to stay in the matrix or the red pill to wake up.
